This is an indirect/dependent primitive: requires external corruption of urandom FILE* at base+0x2070. No BUG in this binary (BUG-001/BUG-002) can reach base+0x2070 to corrupt the FILE*.

primitives.notes: This is an INDIRECT primitive: it requires the urandom FILE* at base+0x2070 to be corrupted to NULL or invalid. Analysis of all other BUGs in this binary shows none can write to base+0x2070: BUG-001's OOB write (buf[-1], 1 byte) for the name buffer reaches base+0x203f (48 bytes before FILE*); BUG-002's strcpy overflow writes toward rbp (away from FILE* at rbp-0x1020); the NUL write at base+(i+5)*0x10 maxes at base+0x1040. Therefore, the CRASH primitive is theoretically valid and dynamically verified via GDB, but cannot be triggered by attacker-controlled input in the current binary without external FILE* corruption.

non_primitives.reason: The uninitialized random_byte is used as an index into the loop2 hash array, but movzx al (at 0x13b2) bounds the index to 0-255, which is exactly the valid range of the 256-slot hash array (base+0x40 to base+0x1040). No out-of-bounds access occurs. The access is always within the allocated stack frame.

The index is bounded to 0-255 by movzx al and always indexes into the loop2 hash array within the stack frame. The attacker cannot control the index value (it comes from uninitialized memory, not attacker input). No arbitrary address read is possible.

BUG-003 involves only a read operation (fread) and a read+print operation (hash leak). No write operation occurs beyond the 1-byte fread write to [rbp-0x8] (which fails when the bug triggers). No arbitrary write primitive is possible from this bug.

unresolved.reason: In normal operation, /dev/urandom always succeeds. No code path in the binary closes the urandom fd or corrupts the FILE*. The fd limit (1024) is far above the few fds used. No attacker input path can close fd 4 or corrupt base+0x2070.
